notes:
Summary: Enterprise evaluation focused on Redwood Dedicated. Primary ask: strong throughput guarantees + deterministic latency behavior under mixed workloads. Prismark runs latency-sensitive personalization and customer support routing; can't accept noisy-neighbor tail latency spikes.

Key requirements (short):
- Throughput: sustain 5k tokens/sec steady-state for reranking pipeline; peak burst target 18k tokens/sec for 1-5 minute windows.
- Latency SLOs: chat/rerank p95 <= 120ms (goal 80ms) for 2k concurrent qps; p99 budget defined per-route.
- Reserved GPU planning: prefer 8x A100-equivalent reserved (primary pool) + 2x A100 burst pool in separate tenant lane.
- Tenant isolation: strict KV/cache separation, dedicated CUDA context per-tenant lane if possible.
- Traffic shaping / priority lanes: per-route priority weights, token-based quotas, emergency preemption policy for high-priority routes.
- Noisy-neighbor controls: auto-throttle per-AE (per-tenant) when GPU scheduling fairness breaches; per-route backpressure and soft quotas + hard limits.
- Routing/fallbacks: fallback to smaller model family with graceful degradation and explicit latency targets.
- Observability: token-level cost & latency breakdown, per-route trace, and tracing hooks for internal APM.

Timeline / recent activity (bullets):
- 2026-01-28: POC kickoff call (Fireflies ff_2026-01-28_prismark_poc_kickoff). Covered reserved capacity needs + initial perf targets.
- 2026-02-03: Sent draft Dedicated topology + pricing (drive://pricing/prismark_dedicated_quote_v2).

- 2026-02-20: Agreed next step: 48h synthetic soak with mixed chat + rerank workloads to validate p95/p99 and throughput. Redwood to provide test harness and suggested configs.

Technical notes from SE (Arjun):
- Proposed config: two isolated GPU pools: primary-reserved (8 gpus) for production-critical routes, burst-reserved (2 gpus) for unpredictable traffic. Use policy-based routing to steer prioritized routes into primary lane.
- Traffic shaping strategy: token-budget per-route (daily/hourly), token-leaky-bucket for smoothing, and priority queues with weight decay. Low-priority requests receive 429s when both soft and hard quotas exhausted.
- Isolation primitives: namespace-level KV caches, separate warmup kernels, and per-tenant CUDA streams where kernel scheduler allows. Also suggested KV cache eviction priority to avoid cross-tenant pollution.
- Noisy neighbor mitigation: per-device QPS caps, early CPU-side admission control, and GPU memory overcommit detection with automatic model shedding to smaller quantized variants.

Procurement & SLA negotiation points (notes):
- Prismark pushing for explicit latency SLOs with financial credits (p95 and p99). Legal wants example credit schedule tied to p99 breaches during business hours.
- They want guaranteed dedicated capacity during maintenance windows; Redwood to propose maintenance fenestration and migration windows.
- Request for 30-day rollback / capacity reconfiguration clause in contract for first quarter after go-live.

POC success criteria (agreed):
- Demonstrate sustained 5k tok/sec for reranking for 24h with p95 <= 120ms.
- Show prioritized route always meets p95 < 100ms under mixed load.
- Validate preemption: when low-priority jobs are present, high-priority route latency does not regress >10% from baseline.

- "If noisy neighbors cause even intermittent SLO breaches, ops will escalate to execs."
